How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Found it through a friend who asked someone we knew had been on exchange and we managed to take over their lease. Use your network or try WG gesucht!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I would say worth it to live closer to the city and commute to uni than live close to campus and commute to the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This was definitely the worst part, very confusing.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You choose more courses than you need and then your able to drop courses within the first weeks. If you didn't get a spot in a course you really wanted, you might be able to join in that same period if someone else decides to drop it and a spot opens up. This is nice because you get to try out different things before you decide, but also very stressful. I ended up taking way to many courses during the first week because I didn't know if I would get a spot on those I really wanted, which was a waste of time. But worth in the end it all worked out and I got the courses I wanted :)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Erasmus office mail was quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Initially I didn't get all the classes I wanted, but it worked out in the end.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for preapproval for all the courses you are considering early.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found out too late that I could actually get BA level courses preapproved, which was a shame. There was not a huge selection of MA courses in English, so knowing that BA courses would be preapproved could have made it easier for me to work out a schedule.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More students engage, less teachers talking.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
- International Order in Crisis? 
- Politics of Trade 
- Ghosts/Haunting Theories in the Politics of the Middle East/North Africa Region
- Lecture Series: US Foreign Policy in Turbulent Times 
- Resilienz demokratischer Systeme 
- Governance in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Politics of Trade - engaged professor.

Lecture Series: US Foreign Policy in Turbulent Times  and International Order in Crisis? - very relevant for IR interested students.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Unisport + a lot of posters around campus with different activities.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Unisport is nice! Consider checking out ESN_berlin, they have activities for exchange students as well.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Dresden and Leipzig + nature/lakes around Berlin.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Found it pretty easy as a student in CPH-

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Trying out a course in German if you speak it well enough.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Didn't reallly find anything culturally challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Berliners are open and very politically engaged :) A lot of demos and soli partys happening!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Apply for preapproval fast
2. Consider the semester structure (starts and ends later than in CPH)
3. Consider the pre semester language course provided by FU. Seemed like a lot of people made friends there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Most information you need will get sent by FU.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Just making friends and figuring out every day life in Berlin.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Gets a bit lonely sometimes, but that's part of the journey - just embrace it and channel your inner main character !!!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
